# googleplay_track (Resource)

A custom closed testing track of an app.

This resource manages the existence of the track and nothing else. The releases on it are not read, compared or written: builds are expected to be uploaded by a release pipeline.

~> **A track cannot be deleted.** The API has no call for it. Destroying this resource only removes it from state, with a warning, and the track stays in Play Console. Creating a track whose name is already taken fails, so bring an existing track under management with an import.

The built-in tracks (`production`, `beta`, `alpha`, `internal`) always exist and need no resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom closed testing track. Builds are uploaded to it by your release
# pipeline: this resource never reads or writes the releases on a track.
resource "googleplay_track" "qa" {
  package_name = "com.example.app"
  track        = "qa"
}

# A closed testing track for the Wear OS form factor.
resource "googleplay_track" "wear_qa" {
  package_name = "com.example.app"
  track        = "wear:qa"
  form_factor  = "WEAR"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `package_name` (String) The package name (application id) of the app, for example `com.example.app`. The app must already exist in Play Console: the API cannot create one. Changing it creates a new track.
- `track` (String) The identifier of the track. A track of a form factor other than the default carries that form factor's prefix, `wear:` or `automotive:`, for example `wear:qa`. Changing it creates a new track.

### Optional

- `form_factor` (String) The form factor of the track: `DEFAULT`, `WEAR`, `AUTOMOTIVE`. Defaults to the form factor the prefix of `track` names, `DEFAULT` when there is none. Changing it creates a new track.
- `type` (String) The type of the track. `CLOSED_TESTING` is the only type the API can create, and the default.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `{package_name}/{track}`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = googleplay_track.qa
  id = "com.example.app/qa"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a track by package name and track identifier.
tofu import googleplay_track.qa com.example.app/qa
```
